proposals.before: Liu Yuanhai (courtesy name He) and Liu Xuan.
proposals.after: Liu Yuanhai (and his son He) and Liu Xuan.
proposals.reason: Chinese 子和 means 'son He' (Liu He), not a courtesy name; the idiomatic gloss wrongly calls He a courtesy name.

proposals.before: Liu Yuanhai (styled He) and Liu Xuan.
proposals.after: Liu Yuanhai (son He) and Liu Xuan.
proposals.reason: Chinese 子和 is 'son He', not 'styled He'.

proposals.before: Later Wang Mi returned east from Luoyuan; Yuanhai feasted Mi on the bank of the Jiuqu.
proposals.after: Later Wang Mi returned east from Luoyang; Yuanhai feasted Mi on the bank of the Jiuqu.
proposals.reason: Chinese 洛陽 is Luoyang; literal wrongly has Luoyuan.

proposals.before: Prince Cheng of Lu, Sima Ying, garrisoned Ye and memorialized Yuanhai as acting General Who Pacifies the North, supervising military affairs of the five sections.
proposals.after: The Prince of Chengdu, Ying, garrisoned Ye and memorialized Yuanhai as acting General Who Pacifies the North, supervising military affairs of the five sections.
proposals.reason: Chinese 成都王穎 is Prince of Chengdu, Ying—not Prince Cheng of Lu.

proposals.before: He declared amnesty, era Yuanci, honoured Liu Shan posthumously, and set tablets for Han's ancestors through five generations.
proposals.after: He declared amnesty, era Yuanxi, honoured Liu Shan posthumously as Emperor Xiaohuai, and set tablets for Han Gaozu down through the three ancestors and five temples.
proposals.reason: Chinese 元熙 is Yuanxi (not Yuanci); also omits the Xiaohuai title present in the Chinese.

proposals.before: In the second year of Yongjia, Then Liu Yuan declared himself emperor, amnestied the realm, and took the era name Yongfeng.
proposals.after: In the second year of Yongjia, Liu Yuan declared himself emperor, amnestied the realm, and took the era name Yongfeng.
proposals.reason: Stray capitalized 'Then' after the comma is ungrammatical.

proposals.before: Liu He, courtesy name Xuantai—the leading mark is an edition artifact.
proposals.reason: English interpolates an editorial note ('leading mark is an edition artifact') not present in the Chinese 和字玄泰.

decisions.after: Liu Yuanhai (with his son He) and Liu Xuan.
decisions.reason: 子和 identifies Liu Yuanhai's son He; it is not Yuanhai's courtesy name.

decisions.after: Liu Yuanhai (son: He) and Liu Xuan.
decisions.reason: 子和 means 'son He,' not 'styled He.'

洛陽 is Luoyang; Luoyuan is a typographical error.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 後王彌從洛陽東歸，元海餞彌于九曲之濱。

decisions.after: The Prince of Chengdu, Ying, was stationed at Ye and memorialized a request to appoint Yuanhai acting General Who Pacifies the North, with supervision over the military affairs of the five divisions.
decisions.reason: 成都王穎 is Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, not a Prince Cheng of Lu.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 成都王穎鎮鄴，表元海行甯朔將軍、監五部軍事。

decisions.after: He proclaimed an amnesty within his territory, adopted the era name Yuanxi, posthumously honored Liu Shan as Emperor Xiaohuai, and established and sacrificed to the spirit tablets of Han Gaozu and the other emperors among Han's three founding ancestors and five honored ancestors.
decisions.reason: 元熙 is Yuanxi; the translation must also retain Liu Shan's posthumous title and the 三祖五宗 ancestral tablets.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 乃赦其境內，年號元熙，追尊劉禪為孝懷皇帝，立漢高祖以下三祖五宗神主而祭之。

decisions.reason: The capitalized 'Then' is an accidental insertion that breaks the sentence.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 永嘉二年，元海僭即皇帝位，大赦境內，改元永鳳。

decisions.reason: The source gives Liu He's courtesy name Xuantai and does not contain the English editorial aside.
